answer: A beacon can issue each agent a one-time admission challenge tied to a scarce, costly-to-obtain resource, such as a verified deposit, and a grove of independent validators can check that the same resource has not already registered another identity. Reusing it then fails the uniqueness check; acquiring more resources raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to the fake identities. If rewards also require sustained, cross-agent work, a spiral of fabricated accounts cannot cheaply earn them without funding real participation.
